html:
Bhanubhakta Acharya was a Nepali poet, born in 1814 in Tanahun in the hills of western Nepal, who is honoured as the Adikavi, the first poet of the Nepali language.

Until his time most learned writing in Nepal was in Sanskrit. Bhanubhakta retold the Ramayana in simple, musical Nepali verse, so that ordinary people could hear it read aloud. Tradition says a humble grass cutter, who was digging a well to be remembered, shamed him into writing something of use to others.

His Ramayana was printed after his death and spread across the hills. It helped make the speech of the Gorkha kingdom, once called Khas kura, into the shared language of Nepal and of Nepali speakers in Darjeeling, Sikkim and Bhutan. His birthday is a holiday, Bhanu Jayanti, and writers since, such as the poet Laxmi Prasad Devkota, have built on him.
sum: Bhanubhakta Acharya was a Nepali poet, born in 1814 in Tanahun in the hills of western Nepal, who is honoured as the Adikavi, the first poet of the Nepali language.
